Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Sudden-onset severe unilateral (left-sided) headache beginning ~4 hours ago; no clear precipitating trigger identified.  
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Headache began suddenly this morning, intensity rated 6/10 (kidney-stone pain = 10/10).  
  • Persistent despite paracetamol taken ~3 hours ago.  
- ENT symptoms: 
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: not reported.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: not reported.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: not reported.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: blurred vision with “zig-zag” lines.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: not reported.  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: not reported.  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes, neck pain/swelling: not reported.  
- Additional associated symptoms:
  • Dizziness.  
  • Nausea with two episodes of vomiting at headache onset; ongoing nausea.  
  • No limb weakness, gait disturbance, or other focal neurological deficits reported.  
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No previous similar headaches.  
  • History of kidney stones (pain used as reference).  
  • No prior ED visits or injections for similar complaints.  
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food allergies: none known.  
  • Current medication: paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) – no relief.  
  • No regular prescribed medications.  
- Social context:
  • Consultation conducted via telehealth; no mention of accompaniment/supervision at home.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: not observed/reported.
- Airway/breathing: no stridor or respiratory difficulty reported.
- Mental status: alert, oriented; expresses concern about serious intracranial pathology.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with patient: not stated.

Assessment:
- Probable migraine with aura (unilateral headache, visual disturbance, nausea/vomiting, family history of migraine).  
- No current red-flag neurological features elicited.  
- No ENT airway involvement.

Plan:
- Pharmacologic: advised trial of ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) ± over-the-counter anti-emetic and sugary carbonated drink (e.g., cola) as first-line migraine regimen.
- Follow-up: in-person appointment arranged for today for full neurological examination; patient instructed to cancel if symptoms resolve.
- Escalation instructions: seek urgent medical attention if headache worsens, vision changes progress, new weakness/numbness, speech difficulty, balance problems, or vomiting persists (exact wording not provided in transcript).
- Reassurance provided regarding typical migraine presentation and variable age of onset.
